feedback.problem:
Using the fact that ${75}^{∘}={135}^{∘}-{60}^{∘},$
calculate the **exact** value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡{75}^{∘}.$

$\operatorname{sin}⁡({75}^{∘})=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $x={135}^{∘}$ and $y={60}^{∘},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡{75}^{∘} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({135}^{∘}-{60}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡{135}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{60}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡{135}^{∘}\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}-(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
